Command: The high priest shall not defile himself for the dead, even father or mother
Summary: The command: The high priest shall not defile himself for the dead, even father or mother (Leviticus 21:11). The high priest, bearing the crown of the anointing oil, might not defile himself even for his father or mother.
Commandment: The high priest shall not defile himself for the dead, even father or mother.
Application: It cannot be practised as written without the standing temple and Aaronic priesthood; its enduring lesson is God's holiness, the cost of atonement, and worship offered exactly as God appoints.
Purpose: Scripture's stated reason: the crown of the anointing oil of his God is upon him (Leviticus 21:12).
Function: The high priest, bearing the crown of the anointing oil, might not defile himself even for his father or mother — a ceremonial law where office outweighed family. Its goal was to keep the anointed high priest wholly set apart, his holiness unbroken even by the deepest family grief. The evil was letting death, even a parent's death, interrupt the holiest office in Israel. It restrained that by forbidding the defilement outright: the crown of the anointing oil stayed on, and the dead were left to others to bury.
